# `gmail.import`

Materialize an agent-submitted batch of your OWN Sent Gmail messages (fetched agent-side via your host Gmail tools; never called from here — no OVT Google credentials) into the local gmail_export directory. Authorship is verified server-side per message: each message's from and any Sender address must match author_email ignoring case; labels must include SENT and exclude DRAFT/CHAT, and Auto-Submitted must be no when present. Only own text is stored. Accepts the {author_email, sync_cursor, messages} envelope inline or via --file; the CLI also falls back to stdin if neither is given.

- **group:** `mutation`
- **posture:** `reversible`
- **CLI:** `operator-voice gmail-import`
- **MCP tool:** `gmail_import` (mutation — hidden unless explicitly enabled)

## Arguments

| name | type | required | help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `author_email` | `str` | optional, default=None | Your own email address (self-asserted; verified per-message server-side) |
| `messages` | `json` | optional, default=None | JSON list of {message_id, thread_id, internal_date, from, subject, text, labels, sender, auto_submitted}; include label ids, Sender and Auto-Submitted headers when present |
| `sync_cursor` | `json` | optional, default=None | Agent-side Gmail historyId cursor to persist for the next incremental refresh |
| `file` | `str` | optional, default=None | Path to a JSON file containing {author_email, sync_cursor, messages} |

## Examples

```
operator-voice gmail-import < sent-envelope.json
```

## Errors

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `invalid_arguments` | An argument was missing, had the wrong type, or wasn't one of the allowed choices — nothing changed. |
| `author_email_missing` | Your own email address (the top-level author_email) is required — supply it directly, or via --file/stdin as part of the {author_email, messages} envelope. |
| `no_messages_provided` | No messages were supplied — provide --messages, --file, or pipe the envelope via stdin. |
| `import_file_not_found` | No file exists at the given --file path. |
| `import_file_not_valid_json` | The --file content (or piped stdin) was not valid JSON. |
